newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Germany says examining fifth BSE case.
newsitem.headline: Germany says examining fifth BSE case.

text.p: German Farm Minister Jochen Borchert said on Monday that a possible fifth case of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) in Germany was being examined in a cow whose mother was imported from Britain.
Borchert said tests would be completed by the end of the week on whether the animal had BSE, otherwise known as mad cow disease.

"If it's confirmed as BSE it would be a case of maternal transmission. This would lead us to consider whether we have to introduce stricter anti-BSE measures," Borchert told a news conference ahead of a meeting of EU farm ministers.
An EU veterinary committee is due to report in March on whether maternal transmission from cow to calf is possible and how it occurs.
Borchert noted that the previous four German cases of BSE had occurred in cattle imported from Britain, where the disease is most widespread with some 165,000 cases over the past 10 years.
Some people in Germany were calling for the slaughter of all the 3,000 to 5,000 British cattle imported into Germany, he added.
British Farm Minister Douglas Hogg declined comment, saying he didn't have details.

Since the mad cow crisis erupted in March 1996 with Britain's disclosure of a link between BSE and its human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, Germany has taken the toughest stance on protecting public health.

European Union farm ministers, gathering for the first time this year under the new Dutch EU presidency, were due to hear a progress report on discussions on proposals to help restore consumer confidence in beef.
